rules.statement: Never accept or return a grant's hashed token key on an administrative or management surface; address grants by a server-generated opaque identifier instead.
rules.why: The hashed key is derived from the token secret, and putting it in URLs, logs or responses leaks a token identifier. An opaque id keeps the administrative identity separate from the runtime secret.
rules.check: Look at management routes, request/response contracts and log calls for grants. Flag any that take, return or log the grant's hashed key or a token-derived lookup key instead of the opaque grant id.

rules.statement: Keep a management projection of a persisted grant to metadata only, and never include the grant's protected payload (claims, tokens, subject material) or its key.
rules.why: The payload is sensitive, and an administrator needs only metadata to triage or revoke. A metadata projection is the least-privilege surface.
rules.check: Look at management resource/DTO types for grants and the code that maps entities to them. Flag any property or mapping that carries the protected payload, a decrypted payload or the hashed key.

rules.statement: Implement grant revocation as an idempotent soft revoke that stamps a revoked timestamp and keeps the row, so that revoking an already-revoked grant changes nothing and still returns 204, and have the runtime treat a revoked grant as inactive.
rules.why: Revocation has to leave an audit trail, and a soft revoke is what makes DELETE idempotent and safe to retry.
rules.check: Look at grant DELETE handlers and revoke methods. Flag hard deletes of grant rows, an error or non-204 status for a grant that is already revoked, and any runtime lookup that ignores the revoked timestamp when it decides whether a grant is active.

rules.statement: Make a bulk grant revocation require at least one filter and answer 400 when none is given, and have the revoked count it reports exclude grants that were already revoked.
rules.why: Revoking a whole tenant is too dangerous for one request, and the required filter prevents an accidental revoke-all.
rules.check: Look at bulk-revoke endpoints that delete or revoke by filter. Flag any that run with no filters, that lack a 400 guard, or that count already-revoked rows in the result.

rules.statement: Don't use EF Core set-based ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete on rows whose concurrency tokens a SaveChanges interceptor manages; load the matching rows, change them and save them through the change tracker.
rules.why: Set-based updates bypass the concurrency-token interceptor and the change tracker, so the token isn't bumped and running instances don't observe the change.
rules.check: Look for ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteUpdateAsync or ExecuteDelete calls on entities that have interceptor-managed concurrency tokens, such as bulk revoke paths.

rules.statement: Make a grant revocation retry when it loses a concurrency race, instead of answering 412 Precondition Failed.
rules.why: A lost race on a grant row is retried for revocations, so a revoke always takes effect.
rules.check: Look at single and bulk grant revoke paths. Flag any that let a concurrency exception surface as 412 or as an error without retrying.

rules.statement: Filter a management list over a security store only through specific, index-backed filter parameters combined with AND, and never through a generic query protocol such as OData or JSON:API, or a client-supplied IQueryable.
rules.why: A query protocol leaks IQueryable, opens a denial-of-service and complexity surface over a security store, and becomes a heavyweight versioned contract.
rules.check: Look at management list endpoints. Flag OData, JSON:API or dynamic query/expression parameters, and filters that no index on the store backs.

rules.statement: Don't expose create or update endpoints on the management API for runtime-minted grants (authorization codes, refresh tokens and similar); offer only list, read and revoke.
rules.why: The token pipeline mints grants, so the administrator only needs to observe and revoke them.
rules.check: Look at grant management handlers. Flag POST, PUT or PATCH routes that create or change runtime grants. Dedicated flows such as RFC 7591 initial access tokens are the exception.
